title_en: Chinese Humor (12/20): Shared Bikes "Occupy" the Sidewalk
note_en: A verb plus 得 plus a result describes how far an action goes, much like English "so... that...": 这堆单车挤得人几乎走不动路 "the bikes were packed so tightly that people could barely walk." The part after 得 can be a whole clause with its own subject (人), or a comparison, as in 动作熟练得像在玩障碍赛 "moving as nimbly as if running an obstacle course." English puts "so" before the adjective; Chinese simply attaches the result after 得.
